column1: # Known cross-language disagreements between src/analytics/ and frontend/src/ (AU-009).
# THIS FILE IS HAND-MAINTAINED. Nothing generates it, and nothing may. It is the
# only way a key can be excused from golden/expected.tsv, so a new divergence
# cannot be absorbed by re-running a tool -- a person has to write the line, name
# both values, and defend it in review. Both suites hold each language to its own
# recorded value here, so fixing a divergence turns that language red until the
# line is deleted and the golden regenerated. A ledger entry is a record, not a mute.
# Columns: key <TAB> python <TAB> typescript <TAB> note
# Every line below has one root cause, measured rather than assumed:
#   Python's round() breaks an exact tie to the nearest EVEN integer.
#   JavaScript's Math.round() breaks it UPWARD, toward +Infinity.
# The two implementations therefore disagree whenever a quotient lands exactly
# on a half. Three call sites reach it:
#   _pace / pace     int(round(sec / km))       vs Math.round(sec / km)
#   round(v, 2)      round(v, 2)                vs Math.round(v * 100) / 100
#   downsample       round(i * step)            vs Math.round(i * step)
# Measured breadth over the constructed probe space: 1000 of 4001 half-integer
# pace quotients differ; 865 of 20001 three-decimal values differ under round-2;
# 274 of 1275 realistic (n, limit) downsample pairs pick a different item.
# Measured reachability on the repository's own 365-run export: ZERO of 3098
# emitted values differ, and no (n, 150) downsample pair differs at all -- 150 is
# the API default. That is why this has never been noticed, and it is exactly
# what makes it worth pinning: the data that would expose it has not arrived yet.
# These are not one-ULP artefacts. A visitor sees 500 s/km in api mode and
# 501 s/km in static mode for the same run, and a three-point track request
# returns a different GPS sample. Deciding which language moves is NOT this
# ticket's call: `builder.downsample` sits on the byte-identical export path
# (src/export/records.py), so Python cannot move there without changing the
# published bytes, which points at the TypeScript side -- but that changes
# numbers the static dashboard already shows, so it is handed back deliberately.
